def score(item: int, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Score each bin for assigning the current item. Higher score = preferred bin.

    Args:
        item: size of the current item to assign
        bins: remaining capacities of feasible bins (all >= item size)
    Returns:
        scores: priority scores for each bin
    """
    if item == 0:
        return np.zeros_like(bins)

    prime_numbers = np.array([2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17])
    ratios = bins / item
    distance_to_prime = np.min(np.abs(ratios[:, np.newaxis] - prime_numbers), axis=1)
    closest_prime = prime_numbers[np.argmin(np.abs(ratios[:, np.newaxis] - prime_numbers), axis=1)]
    harmonic_term = 2 / (ratios + closest_prime + 1e-6)
    weighted_harmonic = harmonic_term / (distance_to_prime + 1e-6)
    weighted_harmonic[bins > 3 * item] *= 0.1  # Penalty for bins too large
    weighted_harmonic[bins == item] = float('inf')  # Perfect fit gets highest priority
    return weighted_harmonic
genes.thought: The new algorithm scores bins based on the inverse harmonic mean of the ratio and the distance to the nearest prime, with a penalty for bins that are significantly larger than the item and an elevation for bins that are just slightly larger (close to 1).
